preview: An interview experience sharing the online assessment, technical round, and HR round for an internship at Morgan Stanley by Atharva Humane.
content: Morgan Stanley Interview Experience Atharva Humane T.Y. B.Tech Computer Engineering 2022-26 Before the Mid-Semester Tests, TPO sent us an email about the recruitment drive by Morgan Stanley. The online assessment was scheduled for September 10th, followed by the interviews on September 13th. This was unexpected, as we thought that the company wouldn’t visit. Eligibility Criteria: 1. Students from circuital branches. 2. A minimum CGPA of 7.5. 3. No active backlogs. Online Assessment: The assessment was conducted on the SHL AMCAT platform on September 10th. It consisted of three sections: Coding Section: ● Question 1: This task involved working with N encrypted integers, which needed to be decrypted by multiplying all the numbers together and then finding their distinct prime factors. These prime factors would be the final answer. The difficulty was LC-Easy/Medium ● Question 2: It was a standard Sliding Window question. We are given a string of lowercase alphabets. We need to find and print the length of the longest substring that contains the maximum number of distinct vowels. Difficulty was LC-Easy/Medium. ● Question 3: I don't remember this question clearly but it involved a matrix and had something to do with Stage Light Intensity. Difficulty was LC-Medium/Hard. I managed to do the first two questions and the third solution gave TLE. Debugging Section (20 minutes): ● We could choose between Java, C++, and Python. ● It consisted of seven debugging questions. Aptitude Section (36 minutes, 24 questions): The time was limited for this section. I tried to answer the questions but in the end had to make guesses due to the time limit. The online assessment results were announced on September 12th, a day before the interviews. Out of all the participants, 23 students were shortlisted for the interview rounds. Interview: The interview with Morgan Stanley was conducted online on Zoom and started at 8 AM. Round 1: My interview was scheduled for 10 AM, and there were two panelists for the first round. They began by introducing themselves and then asked me to introduce myself. ● The first question was a DSA problem involving reversing an array using an extra array. I provided a solution with a time complexity of O(n/2). ● The second question was to find the smallest positive number in an array. I explained both the O(n) approach for an unsorted array and the O(log n) approach if the array was sorted. They seemed satisfied with my answers. For both questions they asked to code it in a notepad or gdocs. ● Next, they asked me about my third project, which involved ML. I explained that I collaborated with a teammate proficient in ML, read the documentation, and implemented the backend using FastAPI. They asked why I chose FastAPI over alternatives. I explained that Node.js wasn’t convenient for ML integration due to a lack of frameworks, and I had narrowed my choices to FastAPI and Flask as Python has better compatibility with ML and later chose FastAPI. ● They then moved on to DBMS-related questions: ○ What is SQL and NoSQL? Their full forms and differences? ○ Structured vs. Unstructured data. ○ Platforms offering SQL and NoSQL services. ○ Whether structured data can be stored in NoSQL. ○ Examples of structured and unstructured data. ● The discussion shifted to backend implementation. I explained routing in the backend, and how the database connections work. They asked about common HTTP request protocols so I listed common HTTP request methods: GET, PUT, POST, DELETE. They asked if there were more, and I mentioned PATCH but wasn’t sure about others. ● One question was whether replacing all PUT routes with POST would work. I explained that it would, with some debugging, as the underlying logic could be adjusted, but readability and best practices would be compromised. ● They asked if I knew about idempotence. I wasn’t familiar with the term, so they explained it and then asked which HTTP methods were idempotent. I gave a partially correct answer. ● For the next DSA question, they asked me to implement prime factorization using recursion. My initial implementation failed on a test case, but I debugged it, and it worked. I mentioned the time complexity was logarithmic. They also asked me to code it. ● They then asked about deadlock. I explained it using a cyclic wait diagram and suggested the Banker's Algorithm and Semaphores as a solution. They asked how Banker’s Algorithm works. Next they asked how to handle a deadlock once it has occurred, and I explained options like killing processes or ignoring it, as modern OS often do. ● The final question involved SQL. They gave me two tables and asked for a query to find the student with the highest marks in every subjects. My initial solution displayed only the name of the topper in every subjects. Realizing my mistake, I clarified the question again. They mentioned it was fine as we were running out of time. At the end, they asked if I had any questions. (Try asking questions about the company. Their PPT might help with this.) The interview lasted slightly over an hour. It felt intense but I believe I gave my best effort. HR Round: Round 2: This round lasted for about 30 minutes. The second round began with a brief introduction, followed by the interview questions. ● The interviewer started by asking why I wanted to join Morgan Stanley. I had prepared for this question and explained my reasons. ● Next, I was asked to explain any one of my projects in detail. ● They inquired why I hosted the frontend on Vercel and the backend on Render. I justified my choice based on convenience and the deployment tools provided by both platforms. ● The interviewer then asked about the challenges I faced while working on the project. I described some technical issues and how I resolved them. ● Then he asked: "What would you do if a teammate tried to back out of their responsibilities?" I explained by sharing an example from my project where I resolved such a situation. ● "If you were given unlimited resources, money, and developers, what three things would you improve in your project?" I answered that I would enhance the UI, add more features, and improve the project's security, which I had already identified as an area of concern in my Project. ● He asked whether I would consider switching the project to an app. I agreed that it would make the project more convenient to use than a website. ● A follow-up question was: "Can you name some websites that are better as websites than as apps?" I couldn’t think of any examples immediately, and the interviewer reassured me. He then explained that user-targeted applications are often better as apps, while applications used by corporations or companies for commercial purposes are usually better as websites. Finally, he asked if I had any questions for him. I asked him a few questions. Then there was a casual talk about the company’s work culture and the internship. The results were announced at 8 PM. Out of 9 candidates, 8 were selected, and I was fortunate to be among them. Interview Preparation Tips 1. Know every detail on your resume. Use online tools and check the resume’s ATS score. 2. Do not lie on your resume. 3. Try not to stay quiet during the interview. Keep expressing your thought process to the interviewer. 4. Clarify questions before answering. 5. Practice coding and attend contests regularly. Solve problems from LeetCode, GFG, Codeforces, CodeChef 6. Study system design concepts— OOPS, OS, DBMS, basic HLD, and LLD. 7. Take mock interviews with seniors, and peers, or use online platforms for practice. 8. Read past interview experiences to understand common patterns and expectations. 9. Solve at least one problem daily to maintain momentum. 10. Ask seniors about their experiences like what to do and what not to. 11. Learn from your mistakes. If you failed in an Interview let it be HR or Technical, try to find out what went wrong. Resources 1. DSA- NEETCODE150, STRIVERA2Z, GFG, LEETCODE 2. CP- CP31SHEET, CODEFORCES, CODECHEF, ACDLADDER, CSES 3. DBMS- PLAYLIST, QUERYPRAC, GFGDBMS, WHIM 4. OOPS- OOPSCPP, OOPSJAVA, WHIM 5. OS- PLAYLIST, OSGFG, WHIM 6. OTHERS- QB, HR
